sections.answer: Less concentration: the non-audit services ban covering all large companies and PIEs, break-up of the Big Four, joint audits. Lower audit quality: the audit-only split of UK firms, an NAO-style national auditor

sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: a membership filter across Deloitte's ratings and Grant Thornton's statements about the same measures, with members split between Grant Thornton's reply and its annex; medium. Measured: rev 0 (one ask, independence benefit, annex only) "In band — Easy tier", Low 2/5 (Platform validation); rev 1 unmeasured.
- Repair in rev 1 (2026-10-12), from Run 2's traces (Feedback log). What separated the five easier-solver attempts on rev 0 was one thing: the two that found Grant Thornton's annex at the end of Doc 4 were right, the three that did not were wrong. The annex-finders used only the annex and solved the announced cross-reference; the others used only the reply. So rev 0 could be answered from one place. Rev 1 changes the condition so that neither place is enough: the concentration list needs two annex rows (L840, L877) and one reply sentence (L349), and the audit-quality list needs two annex cost lines that sit after page breaks (L849, L909). "anywhere in its response" states that scope. The Deloitte side (seven measures rated High then Low) is unchanged; all five attempts read it correctly.
- Dependency plan: D02 L391-436 -> seven measures rated High then Low. D04: concentration credited to row 2 (L839-840), row 9 (L877) and, in the reply, joint audit (L349, also L32, L286); denied for the split (L28, L843), tendering (L133) and ring-fencing (L299); a cap (L338) fails D02's rating (L400 "High High High"). Audit quality warned for row 3 (L849) and row 15 (L909) only.
- Universe (the seven measures of Step 1). Tendering and rotation reform: neither list (L133 "Alone, it may not reduce market concentration"; annex L883 "could free up the market over time" does not speak of concentration; no quality warning). All-clients prohibition: concentration (L840); no quality warning (its benefit is "encourages investment in audit quality", L838). Audit-only split: not concentration (L28, L325, L843); quality (L849). Joint audits: concentration (L349); no quality warning (L349 "more technical knowledge, quality"). Break-up: concentration (L877); no quality line. Insurance-based system: neither (L900-903). NAO-style auditor: not concentration; quality (L909).
- Necessity: D02 is the only source of ratings; without it the seven are unknown and the market share cap (which D04 says would reduce concentration) cannot be excluded. D04 is the only source of Grant Thornton's statements. Other documents' views on these measures (for example D06 L172-228) are not Grant Thornton's. No removal probes run (optional diagnostics, none requested).
- Bundle independence: five named measures in two groups; a guess would have to place each of the seven correctly. Rev 0's closed-book attempt on this bundle answered "joint audit and market share caps" and was marked as needing the documents.
- Selected-lever checks (which-items): decoys named in the reasoning. Concentration: the market share cap (D04 L338, fails D02's rating), tendering (L133 denies it), the split (L843 "no impact"). Audit quality: tendering (L149 "In spite of ... a reduction in the quality of audit", not blamed), the cap (L347 "possible without destabilising audit quality"), Deloitte's own warnings about the split, break-up and wider prohibition (not Grant Thornton's). Without Deloitte's rating condition the cap joins the first list.
- Targeted failure modes: (1) Linking across documents: annex alone gives "all-clients ban, break-up" for concentration; reply alone gives "joint audits". Both are incomplete. (2) Document convention: L849 and L909 follow the page headers "2 / Measure Costs Benefits" and "5 / Measure Costs Benefits" and precede the next numbered row (4, 16); read as belonging to the next row, the split or the NAO-style auditor drops out of the quality list. Seen in Run 2 on rev 0 (not this wording): three of five easier attempts never located the annex; the two that did used it alone; one of them briefly attached row 15's continuation to row 13 before correcting. Align both modes with the next run's observed wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: not applicable (no arithmetic). Every evidence quote found once in docs/ by script (D02's "Break-up of the four largest firms into smaller audit firms" occurs twice, so the rating line is quoted for c2 instead).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: searched D04 for "concentrat", "dynamic", "free up the market", "market composition" and for "quality" near reduce / undermine / destabilise / erode / impair / detriment (2026-10-12); every hit is classified in the Universe line or concerns no measure. The bundle overview mentions neither table nor these statements.
- Precision/readings: "could" covers the hedged annex entry for the all-clients ban ("potentially leading to") and "does appear to have created" for joint audit. "anywhere in its response" covers reply and annexes. Row 2 also lists a cost in the other direction ("Reduces the incentive for non-Big 4 to enter the large company audit market"); the question asks what Grant Thornton says could happen, and the benefit entry says it. "reduce or destabilise audit quality" uses the two annex verbs so that workload or cost entries (insurance) and capacity entries (joint audits) do not count.
- Completeness: no known source gaps (10 of 10 documents read in full; hashes match the capture).
- Style/set review: plain wording, organisations named, no file or page references; 50 words, two parallel asks. q01 (dropped) shares no input; sketch i08 shares the tendering row and stays unused.
- Warnings answered: origin claude (the form's authorship tick is the user's). list-items: item names contain "and"; the two lists are labelled and comma-separated and equal the five components.

sections.question: Of the CMA's potential measures that Deloitte rates High for costs and Low for benefits, which, if any, does Grant Thornton say anywhere in its response could leave the audit market less concentrated, and which does it warn could reduce or destabilise audit quality? Give each list in any order.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 2, summary table of measures in the appendix): Deloitte gives each measure a rating for costs, then benefits, then implementation challenges. The measures rated High for costs and Low for benefits are: reform of mandatory tendering and auditor rotation, prohibiting non-audit services to all large clients and PIEs, splitting UK firms into audit-only and non-audit practices, joint audits, break-up of the largest firms into smaller audit firms, an insurance-based system, and an NAO-style national auditor.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 4, annex of costs and benefits, one numbered row per measure): the row for prohibiting non-audit services to any other large company or PIE lists as a benefit that other firms can grow, "potentially leading to less audit market concentration and more competition". The row for breaking up the largest firms lists "Immediate impact on market concentration".
Step 3. Source input (Doc 4, reply on the market share cap and joint audits): joint audit is common in France, and "This does appear to have created a more dynamic and less concentrated market". The annex row for joint and shared audits says nothing about concentration, so this member comes from the reply and not from the annex.
Step 4. Check (Doc 2 and Doc 4): no other measure in Step 1 is said to cut concentration. The audit-only split leaves "no impact to market concentration"; of more regular tendering Doc 4 says "Alone, it may not reduce market concentration"; the rows for the insurance-based system and the NAO-style auditor do not mention concentration. Doc 4 does say a market share cap would reduce concentration, but Doc 2 rates that measure High for benefits, so it is not in Step 1.
Step 5. Source input (Doc 4, same annex): the costs of the audit-only split continue after a page break and include "Loss of access of some technical specialisms and restricting talent pool, potentially reducing audit quality." The costs of the NAO-style auditor also continue after a page break and include the loss of partners and staff and "likely destabilisation of audit quality, particularly in very large companies".
Step 6. Check (Doc 4): no other measure in Step 1 carries such a warning. Joint audits are credited with better quality, the all-clients prohibition with more investment in audit quality, and the rows for the break-up, tendering reform and the insurance-based system do not mention audit quality. Doc 4 notes a fall in audit quality "In spite of an increase in tendering and auditor rotation", which does not blame tendering.
Final answer (Doc 2 and Doc 4): Less concentration: the non-audit services ban covering all large companies and PIEs, break-up of the Big Four, joint audits. Lower audit quality: the audit-only split of UK firms, an NAO-style national auditor.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Document convention
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 4's annex credits the all-clients ban and break-up with less concentration, its reply credits joint audits; one place alone gives a partial list. Document convention: the split's and NAO auditor's quality costs follow page breaks in the annex; assigned to the next row, a member drops.
